source_text.body:
Triage email into an urgency-ranked morning summary
An OpenClaw agent via Telegram sends a morning summary organized by urgency and flags same-day responses; the user notes it still makes mistakes and needs spot-checking.
·
Apr 1, 2026
Done with
OC
OpenClaw
What they did
The user ran an OpenClaw agent through Clawdi on Telegram for a couple of months. For inbox triage, the agent pulled from actual email threads and delivered a morning summary organized by urgency, with messages needing a same-day response broken out separately; the user still spot-checks because it sometimes misclassifies things.
How it went
It let the user stop opening email first thing and avoid starting from zero each morning. The source gives no hard metrics, and the main limitation stated is that it still makes occasional mistakes.
Worth knowing
The practical catch is reliability: the user says it still needs spot-checking because it occasionally gets the triage wrong.
Try it yourself
with
OpenClaw
Copy prompt
Each morning at [time], go through my inbox on [email account] and send me a summary on [Telegram or other chat app] sorted by urgency, with anything needing a reply today flagged at the top. Include the sender and a one-line reason for each ranking so I can spot-check your judgment. Do not reply to, archive, or delete any email; only report to me.
Original source: https://www.reddit.com/r/OpenClaw_Tips/comments/1slgszx/things_i_dont_do_manually_anymore_since_setting
